recipes.name: Watergate Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant pistachio pudding mix
1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple, with juice

steps.text: Combine crushed pineapple with juice, instant pudding mix, mini marshmallows, and walnuts in a large serving bowl. Mix until well combined.
Fold in whipped topping, then chill for 1 to 2 hours before serving.
When ready to serve, garnish with crushed pistachios and maraschino cherries.

raw_recipe.headline: Watergate Salad
raw_recipe.description: Watergate salad made with pistachio pudding, pineapple, marshmallows, walnuts, and whipped topping; serve as either a side salad or dessert.

video.description: This classic Watergate salad has mini marshmallows, walnuts, and pistachio pudding! Top with cherries for a sweet treat!

review.reviewBody: Added 20 oz crushed pineapple and the whole 8 oz whipped topping container as many sugested. I took this to a baby shower and as soon as i put it on the table i saw someone else had brought one also. I was a little dissapointed about that BUT as i saw more and more people going to my bowl over and over and saying "whatever this is, it's good!" i knew the bowl was going to be empty soon. When we cleaned up at the end of the shower , my bowl was in fact empty and the other lady's was almost full. I felt a little bad about that, but hey, if it's better what can you do? LOVE the nuts in it!

This is a good recipe that needs some modifications. To get the pineapple to pudding mix ration right, I make it with a 20 ounce can of fruit with two boxes of pudding, adding double the whipped cream. Sometimes it is good to add coconut as well.

Easy and so good! I would add more pineapple than called for - I used a 20-oz. can of (unsweetened) pineapple chunks. The second time I made this, I wanted to make it less soupy (adding all the juice was just too much liquid), so I drained the entire 20-oz. can of pineapple (chunks) into a measuring cup, then added 1/2 cup juice to the pudding. Letting it sit overnight is key, as it will taste too much like unprepared pudding if you don't. I used pecans instead of walnuts, and cut down on the amount (used 1/4 cup instead of 1/2), and would do that again. I also used the entire 8-oz. tub of whipped topping. Thanks for the recipe!

my mom made this every holiday and called it pistacio pudding. She didn't add nuts; however, I do endorse the addition of some type of finely chopped nuts. We also never added the marshmallows so for those who don't appreciate the added sweet, you won't notice the absence of those. i would also support draining the crushed pineapple to avoid soupyness. 
The major difference in my mom's recipe would be the addition of minced maraschino cherries. For me this is a key ingredient. All in all...no holiday dinner is complete without this pudding/salad.

Reviewing the dish, not the recipe. Mix a box of pistachio pudding into a 20 oz can of crushed pineapple (including juice) Add in 1 cup marshmallows, 1/2 cup chopped nuts. And lastly fold in one 8oz tub whipped topping. Put it in the fridge for a couple of hours. Top with maraschino cheerios.

I make this often but I add vanilla yogurt to the recipe. Mix the pistachio pudding with the canned pineapple first to disolve the pudding then add the marshmallows, nuts and whipped topping last.You can also make this have less sugar by using sugar free pudding mix, sugar free whipped topping and eliminating the marshmallows. It's very good!

I'll make this, but I'd NEVER use Cool Whip fake whipped cream! Always use REAL freshly whipped cream from extra heavy cream I whip up with my mixer. No mini marshmallows. I'll use pineapple, coconut and walnuts and serve it with some banana slices around the bowl but DON'T put the bananas in the salad unless it's all going to be eaten same day or they'll start turning dark brown and get mushy.

I agree with other cooks/users: Adding Coconut just gives this mixture the added plus that it begs for. Also, for a pretty red accent to the green concoction here, add a small qty to your Watergate Salad ... but *do* make sure you drain and dry the cherries before adding. Save a few to decorate the top of this sweet salad delight.

I don’t like pistachios and I have never made this before. It was requested by a friend who’d just lost his Father. SO, I wanted it to be good. I loved the results! It was delicious! My alterations of the recipe were: Pecans versus walnut, ~ 3/4 cups. I toasted the Pecans with Coconut Oil. I folded in 6-7 ounces of Cool Whip. I topped the salad with a dollop of whip cream and a few toasted pecans

I use 20 oz crushed pineapple and double the pudding, used a whole 8 oz tub of cool whip. 5 stars is for EXACT recipe. I just enjoy my changes. Edit: someone said it tastes fine without marshmallows. I’m gonna do that next time because I don’t like the kinda mushy marshmallows on the second day.

Only thing I add an extra box of 1ounce pudding and a block of cream cheese and a can of mandarin oranges and a can of pineapple chunks as well and a whole 8 ounces of whip cream and a lot more nuts than it calls for I love the walnuts
Such a great recipe. You will love it!! Desert or a snack, but won't make you feel like it's all bad for you lol 😂
I make this several times a year ! Everyone asks me to bring this to family parties.
Addicted, obsessed all of the above.

My father used to make this for every family get together starting in the early 80's. It was definitely a family favorite. It has been many years since we've had it, and I made it for our Easter get together...it was an instant hit! ... and lots of fond memories of my dad.
I use small curd cottage cheese in place of the cool whip and pecans instead of walnuts. This was my former mother-in-law's recipe. We love this version.

A super simple recipe that taste great. Wouldn’t change a thing.. Need to make it more often. I have made this again taking suggestions about 20oz pineapple, added coconut and used sugar free pudding and cool whip and used pecans instead of walnuts. It was awesome.

I've loved this since I was really little I'm now 57. This salad came about the same time I was born lollllll my mom tried fruit cocktail with this recipe once instead of pineapple and it was really gross don't do it!!!
This recipe called for 8 ounces of pineapple. Every other recipe seems to call for 20. This was way too thick and dry.
This is a keeper! Fam was happy to have this retro salad. Easy and fast to make. Great taste of childhood in 70s.
